    1   Q.     Please state your name and business address.
    2   A.     My name is Gwin Cash. My business address is 321 North Harvey, Oklahoma City,
    3          Oklahoma 73102.
    4
    5   Q.     By whom are you employed and in what capacity?
    6   A.     I am employed by Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E” or “Company”) as
    7          Senior Manager of Pricing, Rate Administration, and Load Analysis.
    8
    9   Q.     Please summarize your professional qualifications and educational background.
   10   A.     I have worked for OG&E in various capacities for over 24 years. I joined the Company’s
   11          regulatory department in January 2015 as the Rate Administration Manager and in July of
   12          2017 I assumed additional responsibilities as the manager of Cost of Service. In May of
   13          2023, I became the manager of Pricing and Rate Administration. In November of 2025, I
   14          became Senior Manager of Pricing, Rate Administration, and Load Analysis. My Pricing
   15          responsibilities include oversight of the department’s development of rates and charges in
   16          the Company’s retail electric tariffs. My Rate Administration responsibilities include
   17          maintaining OG&E’s tariffs on file with the regulatory commissions and ensuring
   18          consistent application of these tariffs in the manner in which they are intended. My Load
   19          Analysis responsibilities include oversight of the research of retail customer electric load,
   20          primarily at the customer, class, and system levels; the construction of the Control Area
   21          Load model; ad-hoc statistical analyses; and retrieval and analysis of customer usage data.
   22          Additional duties include computing rider factors and monthly retail revenue reporting.
   23          Prior to joining OG&E’s regulatory department I worked as a Senior Business Analyst in
   24          OG&E’s Sales and Customer Support department and as a Workforce Analyst in OG&E’s
   25          Customer Service department. I received a Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics
   26          with a Specialization in Computing from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1999.

    1   Q.     What is the purpose of your testimony in this proceeding?
    2   A.     The purpose of my testimony is to sponsor and describe in detail the proposed Extra Large
    3          Power and Light (“XLPL”) tariff and Terms and Conditions of Service for Extra Large
    4          Load Customers (“T&CXLLC”), which I am sponsoring as Direct Exhibits GC-1 and GC-
    5          2, respectively. Specifically, I will walk through each section of both documents and
    6          explain the provisions contained therein, so that the Commission has a complete and clear
    7          understanding of the rates, terms, and conditions under which OG&E proposes to serve
    8          certain large load customers. My testimony is filed in support of OG&E’s request that the
    9          Commission approve the XLPL tariff and the accompanying T&CXLLC 1 as filed herein,
   10          which are consistent with the requirements of Oklahoma House Bill 2992 (“HB 2992”) and
   11          in compliance with the Commission’s Final Order No. 753440 in Case No. PUD2025-
   12          000038.
   13
   14                            EXTRA LARGE POWER AND LIGHT TARIFF
   15   Q.     Please describe the XLPL tariff.
   16   A.     The Extra Large Power and Light tariff, designated as the XLPL tariff, is a new retail
   17          electric service rate schedule proposed by OG&E to serve customers whose electric
   18          demands meet the requirements outlined in HB 2992. The tariff is applicable to any
   19          customer meeting the definition of an Extra Large Load Customer as set forth in the
   20          T&CXLLC, and service under the tariff requires execution of a Preliminary Agreement
   21          (“PA”) and an Electric Service Agreement (“ESA”) as described in those T&CXLLC. As
   22          described in detail below, there are also optional tariffs that are excluded and not
   23          additionally available to XLPL.
   24
   25   Q.     Why is OG&E proposing the XLPL tariff at this time?
   26   A.     The Oklahoma Corporation Commission (“Commission”) ordered OG&E to file for
   27          approval of a new large load tariff by July 1, 2026. 2 HB 2992, which was recently passed
   28          by the Oklahoma legislature, also becomes effective July 1, 2026, and requires electric
   29          utilities to establish and maintain separate terms and conditions of electric service

    2          to such large load customers.
    3
    4   Q.     Please explain how the XLPL tariff differs from OG&E’s existing large commercial
    5          and industrial tariffs.
    6   A.     The XLPL tariff differs from OG&E’s existing large commercial and industrial tariffs in
    7          several respects specific to the rate design and structural provisions of the XLPL tariff.
    8          Fuel cost recovery, and energy-related costs for XLPL customers shall be excluded from
    9          the standard FCA recovery. Instead, XLPL customers will pay the hourly Southwest Power
   10          Pool Day-Ahead Locational Marginal Price for OG&E, adjusted for line losses, while
   11          remaining subject to their allocated share of all capacity and purchased power agreement
   12          costs recovered through the FCA. 3 This treatment stands in contrast to OG&E’s existing
   13          large commercial and industrial tariffs, such as LPL-1 and LPL-TOU, under which the
   14          standard FCAon, FCAoff, and FCAw factors are applied directly to the applicable energy
   15          components of the bill. With respect to minimum billing obligations, the XLPL tariff sets
   16          the billing demand floor at no less than 85 percent of the customer’s Billing Contract
   17          Demand for the applicable billing month.         It also imposes minimum billing energy
   18          obligations as well, with both the minimum billing demand and minimum billing energy
   19          serving as the billing determinants for rate design purposes in any general rate case or fixed
   20          cost recovery rider proceeding. 4,5
   21

   14   Q.     Please explain the “EFFECTIVE IN” section.
   15   A.     This section describes the XLPL tariff as being effective in all territory served by OG&E
   16          in Oklahoma. 6
   17
   18   Q.     Please explain the “APPLICABILITY” section.
   19   A.     This section explains that the XLPL tariff is applicable to any customer meeting the
   20          definition of an Extra Large Load Customer as set forth in the T&CXLLC, which defines
   21          three distinct customer types.
   22              •   Customer Type 1 means any customer beginning service with OG&E after July 1,
   23                  2026, and expected to have an annual peak demand of 75 MW or more.
   24              •   Customer Type 2 means existing customers taking service before July 1, 2026,
   25                  whose future billing demand is expected to either: (a) increase by 75 MW or more
   26                  above their billing demand prior to July 1, 2026, or (b) increases its demand and
   27                  has a total demand of 125 MW or more.
   28              •   Customer Type 3 means existing customers taking service before July 1, 2026, who
   29                  may not be adding load, but whose service conditions are such that OG&E would
   30                  be required to add generating capacity to meet a 75 MW or higher increase in
   31                  demand for that existing customer. 7

    1                 This section also states that the execution of a PA and an ESA is required for
    2          Customer Type 1 and Customer Type 2, as set forth in the T&CXLLC. For Customer Type
    3          3, the execution of a PA and an ESA may be required, at OG&E’s discretion, depending on
    4          the circumstances of service to that customer. 8 All customers that meet one of these
    5          definitions, regardless of type, are required to take service under the XLPL tariff. 9
    6                 Additionally, optional tariff subscriptions are not available to customers taking
    7          service under the XLPL tariff, including the Green Power Wind Rider, Renewable Energy
    8          Program, Utility Solar Program, Load Reduction Rider, Day-Ahead Pricing and Flex Price
    9          schedules, Economic Development Incentive Credit Rider, and the Energizing Renewable
   10          Connections Rider. 10
   11
   12   Q.     Please explain the “PRICING” section.
   13   A.     The “PRICING” Section of the XLPL tariff establishes a pricing structure consisting of
   14          three primary billing components: a monthly customer charge, capacity-based demand
   15          charges, and time-differentiated energy charges, with the specific rates varying by service
   16          level. 11 The pricing structure with respect to the Customer Charge, the Capacity Charge,
   17          and the Energy Charges is identical to that of the Company’s Large Power and Light Time-
   18          of-Use (“LPL-TOU”) tariff in that the Capacity Charge is a fixed year-round charge per
   19          kW per month and the Energy Charges are time-differentiated rates during the Summer
   20          Season and a single rate during the Winter Season. In addition to these charges, there is
   21          also a Customer Class Protection Charge and a Customer Affordability Charge, both of
   22          which are fixed monthly kW charges. 12
   23

   25   A.     The initial prices for the Customer Charge, the Capacity Charge, and the Energy Charges
   26          are the same as the existing Commission approved LPL-TOU rates. The Company is
   27          selecting these prices because the LPL-TOU tariff is the current active tariff for which these

    8   Q.     Please explain the “CUSTOMER CLASS PROTECTION CHARGE” section.
    9   A.     The Customer Class Protection Charge is designed to be developed and updated by OG&E
   10          in each general rate case proceeding, so that if future cost-of-service analysis demonstrates
   11          that the XLPL class is causing adverse rate impacts to other customer classes, the
   12          Commission will have the opportunity and a mechanism to set the charge at an appropriate
   13          level to remedy any potential impact. 14 The charge is currently set at $0 per kW per month
   14          at both Service Level 1 and Service Level 2, meaning no amount will initially be collected
   15          from XLPL customers under this charge at the time the tariff initially takes effect. In this
   16          way, the Customer Class Protection Charge functions as a tariff-embedded fail-safe
   17          mechanism that ensures the cost causation principles required by Oklahoma House Bill
   18          2992 are reviewed often, and enforced on an ongoing basis.
   19
   20   Q.     Please Explain the “CUSTOMER AFFORDABILITY CHARGE” section.
   21   A.     The Customer Affordability Charge is a capacity charge assessed on all XLPL customers
   22          on their Billing Demand at a rate of $2.50 per kW per month, applicable at both Service
   23          Level 1 and Service Level 2. The revenues collected through this charge are placed in a
   24          regulatory liability to be credited to residential customers. 15 It was designed assuming
   25          application to a hypothetical XLPL customer class size of 1 GW and collecting revenues
   26          equivalent to approximately $30 million. This approximates the total costs for the Low
   27          Income Assistance Program (“LIAP”) rider credits, an expansion of the Senior Citizen
   28          Discount credits to all seniors, and approximately twenty percent of the residential portion

    2          collected through the Energy Efficiency Program rider.
    3
    4   Q.     Please explain the “DEFINITION OF SEASON” section.
    5   A.     Consistent with other OG&E tariffs, the XLPL tariff defines the Summer Season as the five
    6          OG&E Revenue Months of June through October, and the Winter Season as the seven
    7          OG&E Revenue Months of November through May. Within the Summer Season, On-Peak
    8          Hours are defined as the period beginning each day at 2:00 p.m. and ending at 7:00 p.m.
    9          local time from June 1 through September 30, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, Juneteenth,
   10          and Independence Day as recognized by OG&E, and Labor Day, with all remaining hours
   11          constituting Off-Peak Hours.       During the Winter Season, no on-peak and off-peak
   12          distinction is made, and a single energy rate applies to all hours. 16
   13
   14   Q.     Please explain the “DETERMINATION OF MAXIMUM DEMAND” section.
   15   A.     This section describes how the Company determines an XLPL customer’s measured actual
   16          maximum demand for each billing period. The customer’s Maximum Demand is the
   17          maximum rate at which energy is used for any period of 15 consecutive minutes of the
   18          month for which the bill is rendered, as shown by the Company’s demand meter. 17 This
   19          15-minute interval measurement standard is consistent with the demand measurement
   20          methodology used across OG&E’s existing commercial and industrial tariffs with demand
   21          rates, including the Large Power and Light, Power and Light, and Public Schools Large
   22          schedules.
   23
   24   Q.     Please explain the “DETERMINATION OF BILLING DEMAND” section.
   25   A.     This section describes how the Company arrives at the Billing Demand value to which the
   26          XLPL tariff Capacity charges will be assessed. The Billing Demand is the Maximum
   27          Demand, corrected for power factor, as set forth under the Power Factor Clause, provided
   28          that the Billing Demand shall never be less than 85 percent of the customer’s Billing

    4          XLPL customer and that this occurs when the customer’s actual measured demand falls
    5          below the contracted level in a given month.
    6
    7   Q.     Please explain the “BILLING CONTRACT DEMAND” section.
    8   A.     This section describes how the Billing Contract Demands are determined for each of the
    9          three customer types served by this tariff. For Customer Type 1 with an ESA, the Billing
   10          Contract Demand is the customer’s expected total load, inclusive of the Contract Demand
   11          in the signed ESA. For Customer Type 2 with an ESA, the Billing Contract Demand is the
   12          customer’s expected total load inclusive of the incremental Contract Demand in the signed
   13          ESA. For Customer Type 3 with an ESA, the Billing Contract Demand is likewise the
   14          customer’s expected total load inclusive of the incremental Contract Demand in the signed
   15          ESA. For Customer Type 3 without an ESA, the Billing Contract Demand is the expected
   16          total Billing Demand of the customer as reasonably determined by OG&E, and OG&E
   17          shall have the right to limit service to such amount. 19
   18
   19   Q.     Please explain the “POWER FACTOR CLAUSE” section.
   20   A.     This section describes how the customer’s Maximum Demand is adjusted when their power
   21          factor falls below 100%. This clause requires that XLPL customers shall at all times take
   22          and use power in such manner that the power factor shall be as nearly 100 percent as
   23          possible, but when the average power factor as determined by continuous measurement of
   24          lagging reactive kilovolt-ampere (kVAr) hours is less than 98 percent, the Billing Demand
   25          shall be determined by multiplying the Billing Demand by 98 and dividing the product thus
   26          obtained by the actual average power factor expressed in percent. All customers under this
   27          schedule are required to have suitable measuring equipment, as reasonably determined by
   28          OG&E, at the metering point to determine the customer’s monthly maximum kVAr. 20 It is

    4          under the XLPL tariff and the correspondingly greater impact that poor power factor can
    5          have on OG&E’s transmission and distribution system when serving customers of this
    6          magnitude.
    7
    8   Q.     Please explain the “DETERMINATION OF BILLING ENERGY” section.
    9   A.     This section describes how the Company determines an XLPL customer’s Billing Energy
   10          upon which the XLPL tariff’s energy charges are based. It is the total energy used during
   11          the billing cycle, provided that the Billing Energy shall not be less than the amount of
   12          energy determined by a 90 percent load factor requirement. Specifically, the minimum
   13          Billing Energy is the greater of: the Billing Demand multiplied by the number of hours in
   14          the billing month multiplied by 90 percent, or the actual measured energy consumption.
   15          When applying the Billing Demand multiplied by hours multiplied by 90 percent
   16          calculation, the determination of on-peak and off-peak energy levels is based on the ratio
   17          of actual on-peak and off-peak usage. If there is no usage for the month, the on-peak and
   18          off-peak split is determined by the on-peak and off-peak averages of the summer billing
   19          months of the prior 12 months; and if there is no usage for the month and no usage for the
   20          prior 12 months, the on-peak usage is determined by using 12 percent for on-peak. 21
   21

   23   A.     The XLPL tariff establishes two service levels under which customers may take service,
   24          with the applicable service level determining the customer, demand, and energy charges
   25          assessed each month. Service Level 1 means service at any nominal standard voltage of
   26          the Company above 50 kV where service is rendered through a direct tap to the Company’s
   27          prevailing transmission source. Service Level 2 means service at any nominal standard
   28          voltage of the Company between 2 kV and 50 kV, both inclusive, where service is rendered
   29          through a Company Substation which has a transmission voltage source and the point of

    8    Q.    Please explain the “METERING ADJUSTMENT” section.
    9    A.    The Metering Adjustment provision of the XLPL tariff addresses the situation in which
   10          OG&E chooses to install its metering equipment on the load side of the customer’s
   11          transformer rather than on the source side. In that circumstance, the metering equipment
   12          does not capture the energy lost in the customer’s transformers, and the tariff therefore
   13          requires that the kWh billed be increased by the amount of those transformer losses to
   14          ensure that OG&E recovers the full cost of the energy it delivers to the customer. Under
   15          Service Level 1, the adjusted kWh are calculated by multiplying the actual kWh by the
   16          ratio of Energy Loss Factor 2 to Energy Loss Factor 1. The applicable Energy Loss Factors
   17          are found on page 102 of the Company’s Terms and Conditions of Service. 23
   18
   19    Q.    Please explain the “APPLICATION OF FUEL COST ADJUSTMENT (FCA)”
   20          section.
   21    A.    The energy-related costs for XLPL customers are excluded from the standard FCA
   22          recovery. In place of the standard FCA charge, XLPL customers will pay a per-kWh charge
   23          that reflects the Southwest Power Pool Day-Ahead Locational Marginal Price for OG&E
   24          for all hours during which the customer consumes energy as adjusted for line losses.
   25          Notwithstanding this exclusion from the standard FCA, XLPL customers remain subject to
   26          their allocated share of all capacity and purchased power agreement costs that are otherwise
   27          recovered through the FCA, and are also subject to minimum Billing Energy obligations
   28          for purposes of that cost recovery. 24     This treatment differs from OG&E’s existing

    5   Q.     Please explain the “LATE PAYMENT CHARGE” section.
    6   A.     The XLPL tariff provides that a late payment charge in an amount equal to 1.5 percent of
    7          the total balance for services and charges remaining unpaid on the due date stated on the
    8          bill shall be added to the amount due, with the due date being 20 days after the bill is
    9          issued. 25 This late payment charge is consistent with the late payment charge applied
   10          across OG&E’s existing retail electric tariffs.
   11
   12   Q.     Please explain the “MINIMUM BILL” section.
   13   A.     The minimum monthly bill under the XLPL tariff is the sum of the Customer Charge, the
   14          Minimum Demand Charges, and the Minimum Energy Charges as computed under the rate
   15          schedule. The minimum monthly bill also applies to minimum billing demand and
   16          minimum billing energy as applied to all applicable rider charges. 26 Minimum Charges are
   17          also described in detail in Section 4.02 of the ESA. 27
   18
   19   Q.     Please explain the “FRANCHISE PAYMENT” section.
   20   A.     The XLPL tariff provides that the stated XLPL rates do not include any amount for
   21          franchise payments levied upon the Company by a municipality and that such franchise
   22          payments will be added as a percentage of charges for electric service to the bills of all
   23          customers receiving service from the Company within the corporate limits of the
   24          municipality exacting said payment. 28      This franchise payment section is typical in
   25          OG&E’s retail electric tariffs.

      501     PURPOSE
              These Terms and Conditions of Service for Extra Large Load Customers shall govern the
              supplying and taking of the Company’s electric service for Extra Large Power and Light
              (“XLPL”) customers for whom the XLPL tariff is applicable. Unless otherwise modified by
              these Terms and Conditions of Service for Extra Large Load Customers, the Company’s General
              Terms and Conditions shall apply.

      502     DEFINITIONS
              “Billing Contract Demand” shall have the meaning ascribed to it in the XLPL tariff.
              “Billing Demand” shall have the meaning ascribed to it in the XLPL tariff.
              “Customer” means any customer or an affiliated set of customers across multiple sites and of
                 Customer Type 1, 2, or 3 (defined below). The Company will exercise reasonable discretion
                 when choosing to aggregate multiple sites or premises for the purpose of designating a
                 Customer as Customer Type 1, 2 or 3, with such discretion based on factors including, but
                 not limited to, premises sharing one or more of the following: common owner(s), a common
                 parent company, common local electrical infrastructure, and common control.
              “Customer Type 1” means any Customer beginning service with OG&E after July 1, 2026 and
                reasonably expected to have an annual peak demand of 75 MW or more.
              “Customer Type 2” means existing Customers taking service before July 1, 2026 whose future
                 billing demand is (i) reasonably expected to increase by 75 MW or more above the billing
                 demand that existed prior to July 1, 2026; or (ii) increases its demand and has a total demand
                of 125 MW or more.
              “Customer Type 3” means existing Customers taking service before July 1, 2026 and who may
                not be adding load but conditions exist such that service to the current customer requires
                OG&E to add 75 MW or more of generating capacity.
              “Minimum Billing Demand” means 85 percent of the Billing Contract Demand for the
                applicable billing month.
              “Minimum Billing Energy” means 90 percent of the Billing Demand multiplied by the number
                of hours in billing month.
